description.narrative: The objective is to improve the access and efficiency of electricity services in Bamako and in other targeted areas in the country.

The objective of the Energy Support Project for Mali is to improve the access and efficiency of electricity services in Bamako and in other targeted areas in the country. There are three components to the project, the first component being transmission and distribution reinforcement and extension. This component is mainly intended to finance: (i) upgrade the electricity transmission line between Segou and Bamako; (ii) upgrade and reinforce 30 kv facilities in the peripheral area of Bamako, including the 150 kkv loop; (iii) upgrade and reinforce low and medium voltage distribution networks in Bamako; and (iv) upgrade and reinforce medium and low voltage distribution networks in areas of, among other, Kati, Segou, Kayes, Mopti, Sikasso, and Koutiala. The second component is the energy efficiency and demand-side management. This component is intended to finance: (a) a residential lighting program to replace incandescent or neon light bulbs with compact fluorescent lamps (CFLs), in urban and rural households; (b) a street lighting program to replace incandescent or neon light bulbs by CFLs and/or high pressure sodium vapor lamps, in key urban and rural centers; and (c) a public facilities' lighting program to replace incandescent light bulbs by CFLs. Finally, the third component is the capacity and institutional strengthening of key sector institutions.

comment.narrative: <p>Target not achieved. The purchase order for the smart meters was raised, but the consignment was not delivered as at the project closing date.</p>

title.narrative: Number of MV/LV transformers installed under the project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded</strong>: Activities of electrification were implemented as planned both in the urban and suburban neighborhoods of Bamako and the four regional cities of Kayes, Koutiala, Sikasso and Ségou.</p>

title.narrative: Number of staff trained under the project (utility, MEE)

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved- </strong>The project supported local and foreign training for staff working with the power utility (EDM-SA), the Ministry of Energy, and the Energy Regulatory Agency. The feedback from the training beneficiaries on the quality and usefulness of the training was overall very positive.<strong> </strong></p>

<p><strong>Partially achieved.</strong> The project supported the installation of public solar lamps as planned, but achievements were short of the target. Moreover, there was no adequate maintenance plan, and sustainability of this source of energy is uncertain.</p>

title.narrative: Transmission lines constructed or rehabilitated under the project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved</strong>-The doubling of the 150 kV Bamako-Fana-Ségou electric line was implemented as planned at project appraisal.</p>

<p><strong>Achieved.</strong> Because the use of CFLs was already generalized in Mali before the launch of the project, the initial target was scaled down, and the new target was achieved as planned.</p>

title.narrative: MV distribution lines constructed or rehabilitated under the project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Largely Exceeded</strong>. Activities to build or rehabilitate the MV electricity distribution network were implemented as planned both in the urban and suburban neighborhoods of Bamako and the four regional cities of Kayes, Koutiala, Sikasso, and Ségou.</p>

title.narrative: Peak load reduction from energy efficiency

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved</strong>. The target was achieved because of overall upgrade and rehabilitation of the transmission and distribution network, particularly in Bamako urban and suburban neighborhoods.</p>

title.narrative: LV distribution lines constructed or rehabilitated under the project

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Exceeded.</strong> Activities to build or rehabilitate the LV electricity distribution network were implemented as planned both in the urban and suburban neighborhoods of Bamako and the four regional cities of Kayes, Koutiala, Sikasso, and Ségou.</p>

<p><strong>Largely Achieved.</strong> The targets were largely exceeded, as beneficiaries more than tripled the target level, reaching the level of 992,400 against a target of 285,950. This performance resulted from the project emphasis on rehabilitating the electricity transmission and distribution infrastructure in Bamako urban and suburban neighborhoods. The project corresponded with a Government policy to expand electricity access.</p>

title.narrative: Increase in the number of households connected by EDM-SA outside Bamako

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Largely exceeded. </strong>The target of connected households outside Bamako amounted to 318,000, representing 167 percent of the target of 190,000. This performance resulted from the project emphasis on doubling the 150 kV Bamako-Fana-Ségou electric line and strengthening the distribution network in the four cities of Kayes, Koutiala, Sikasso and Ségou, and Kati.</p>

title.narrative: Total distribution losses on the interconnected grid

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Partially achieved</strong>: The target was missed by 17 percent, because the power utility has not succeeded to bring under control all efficiency factors that could lead to losses reduction. The power utility does not have a total control on the revenue collection and nontechnical losses.</p>

<p><strong>Largely exceeded.</strong> Achievements reached 156 percent of the expected target, following strides in the expansion of the transmission, distribution, and electrification under the project, which corresponded with the Government’s deliberate policy to promote energy access.</p>

title.narrative: Number of households connected by EDM-SA in Bamako

comment.narrative: <p>The target of connected households in Bamako almost tripled, amounting to 662,000, against a target of 350,000. This performance resulted from the project emphasis on rehabilitating and upgrading the electricity transmission and distribution network in Bamakorban and suburban neighborhoods, and a deliberate Government policy to expand energy access.</p>

title.narrative: Implementation calendar for key activities in annual work program adhered to

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Not Achieved</strong>- The initial calendar was not adhered to, because of inadequate implementation arrangements, and unfavorable political developments, which triggered delays in the project closing occurring 45 months after the original closing date.</p>
<p><strong>Achieved: </strong>A study on the Electricity Sector Investment Master Plan was prepared and approved by the Government.</p>

title.narrative: Planned periodic M&E reports submitted on time (Y/N)

comment.narrative: <p><strong>Achieved</strong>- Overall, the ISRs and the Aide Memoires were prepared on a regular basis and provided a good account of progress toward the project outcome and objectives. ISRs had an annex with the status of PDO indicators.</p>
